gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in Rossen Reports' 20-foot drop onto concrete (page updated 2025-06-02), the $46 Casetify Impact case kept the phone intact while the $99.99 OtterBox case let it crack. Even that test covers the case only: no named reviewer has published a measured strap pull or load figure for any strap case.
standout_why: I opened Camera Lookout (2026-10-20). Its only figure is a maker spec, the Apple Crossbody Strap's 42.5–81.9 in adjustment range, with no load, pull or drop test. I could not open the Wired, Good Housekeeping, AppleInsider, Travel+Leisure or Macworld pages (403, 429 or blocked). Good Housekeeping's title, 'I Tried 25 iPhone Cases-These Are the Ones That Survived Our Drop Tests', suggests a rival already has drop-test results of some kind, so a drop result is probably only partly new. A measured strap pull or load figure would be new, but I could find none tied to a named product: Which?'s September 2026 Newton-meter results are behind its paywall.
decides: This is weak support for the pick. If the shopper wants protection plus a strap, a named drop test favours a Casetify Impact-class case over a pricier OtterBox. It says nothing about the cheap rope-lanyard cases ChatGPT showed (Garcase $12.99, COSTA AVENTURE $26.95, CASEPEACH Dusk $29.99) or about Bandolier, none of which has a named drop or pull measurement. The page can honestly say that strap strength figures are maker ratings, not independent measurements.
candidates: Casetify Impact case + Rope Cross-body Strap

findings.label: Which? strap test method (August 2026)
findings.value: 10 straps tested. Durability: strap fixed to a door handle and pulled with a Newton meter, with force raised slowly to the maximum; pass if strap and cord stay intact. Drop test: phone on strap dropped 5 times. Visible anonymous scores range from 37% to 97%; the 37% strap failed the drop test.
findings.source_title: Which?: Best mobile phone straps and lanyards 2026 (Callum Pears)
findings.note: Tested in August 2026, article dated 22 September 2026. Products tested include the Casetify 2-in-1 Utility Lanyard (£57), Mous, OtterBox 2-in-1 Crossbody Strap, Peak Design Mobile Crossbody Multi-Strap and Cuff, and Pela (£16). Scores per product and the maximum newton figures are members-only, so no score can be tied to a product. This is a UK test with UK prices.
